name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=blit/gfx, descriptor=rectangle). Accurately describes the universal 2D rectangle blit and matches the body (strided per-row memmove). No Ghidra address residue.
purpose: Universal 2D rectangle blit: copies a height x src_w_bytes pixel block from src to dst, advancing each pointer by its own stride per row.
logic_summary: for (row=0; (int32)row < (int32)height; row++) { memmove(dst, src, src_w_bytes); dst += dst_stride; src += src_stride; }. Signed loop bound, so height<=0 copies nothing. The simplest and most-called blit primitive (53 callers); the final composite stage for UI/battle/dialog rendering (e.g. copying the render workspace to the mode13h primary at 0xA0000, snapshot copies, rectangle moves). Binary has a compiler-generated __CHK(0x20) stack-probe prologue (omitted in src).
signature: void fd2_blit_rectangle(uint32 dst, uint32 dst_stride, uint32 src, uint32 src_stride, uint32 src_w_bytes, uint32 height)

params.name: dst
params.semantics: Destination base linear address (memmove dest each row; ESI in binary).

params.name: dst_stride
params.semantics: Bytes to advance dst per row (ADD ESI,EBP each row).

params.name: src
params.semantics: Source base linear address (memmove src each row; EDI in binary).

params.name: src_stride
params.semantics: Bytes to advance src per row (ADD EDI,[ESP+0x20] each row).

params.name: src_w_bytes
params.semantics: Bytes copied per row (the memmove count).

params.name: height
params.semantics: Number of rows; signed compare against the loop counter, so <=0 copies nothing.

notes: Disassembly confirms cdecl 6-arg layout matching the src signature: after __CHK prologue + 4 callee-save pushes, [ESP+0x14..0x28] = dst, dst_stride, src, src_stride, src_w_bytes, height. memmove(dst=ESI, src=EDI, count=[ESP+0x24]). Source comment block (blitspr.c lines 35-69) already precise and correct -> keep, no src edit. Ghidra plate describes the same loop/usage and is consistent -> plate untouched. is_thunk=false. category/emit_action were 'undefined' in the task input but the function is plainly a real game gfx primitive.
